title: Symmetry-reduced IBZ k-points (8) in band_out do not match pyatb head/wing full-BZ k-points (64)
symptom: For the Si k444 symmetry+shrink test the SCF/RPA grid is 4x4x4 Gamma-centered, but after ABACUS symmetry the root band_out contains 8 IBZ k points while the pyatb/head-wing files contain 64 full-BZ k points - two different k-point sets inside one run directory.
root_cause: ABACUS symmetry (with irreducible_sector handling) reduces the 4x4x4 Gamma-centered mesh to 8 irreducible k points written to root band_out, whereas the pyatb head/wing producer writes all 64 full-BZ k points. The two sets are different objects and cannot be compared index-by-index or assumed to have the same length.
minimal_fix: Before diagnosing, read the actual inputs/outputs: count k points in root band_out versus the pyatb/head-wing output, and check whether STRU carries an external ABFS_ORBITAL entry (this Si k444 run used an external ABFS_ORBITAL, not on-the-fly PCA generation).
validation: The k-point counts of the symmetry-reduced ABACUS output and of the pyatb head/wing files are each known and the mapping between them is explicit; STRU shows the ABFS_ORBITAL source so the auxiliary-basis provenance is no longer assumed.
avoid: Do not assume the auxiliary basis was generated on the fly by PCA when an external ABFS_ORBITAL was supplied, and do not compare IBZ-reduced ABACUS output with full-BZ pyatb output as if they were the same k-point list.

parameters.band_out k count: 8 IBZ k points after ABACUS symmetry (Si k444)
parameters.ABFS_ORBITAL: external .abfs present in STRU -> PCA is not the source of the auxiliary basis
